title: The Pronoun Is a Crowd
statement: I arrive as a layered witness: a voice, a body, a city, a garden, and a distant world held in one frame. The repeated faces refuse a single definition of self; “I” is assembled from memory, history, place, and the act of looking back.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Make an image of what the word “I” means when you use it.

notes.note: Build a layered self-image: a cosmic field for inner scale, a city as social identity, a botanical vertical spine, and a centered historical portrait as the speaking “I,” with a flamingo accent for a distinctive silhouette.

The first arrangement has a strong central witness but too much empty black field and rectangular source framing. I’ll add two smaller, medallion-like selves and tighten the hierarchy so the repeated “I” reads as identity assembled from history, culture, and reflection.

actions.title: The Pronoun Is a Crowd
actions.statement: I arrive as a layered witness: a voice, a body, a city, a garden, and a distant world held in one frame. The repeated faces refuse a single definition of self; “I” is assembled from memory, history, place, and the act of looking back.

notes.note: The canvas reads clearly as a constellation of selves, but the central portrait’s pale rectangular paper edge interrupts the botanical/cosmic field. I’ll trim it to the figure’s silhouette so the historical witness is embedded rather than pasted on, then inspect the result.

The visual read is strong, but the plant currently appears as a hard white rectangle and the city is only visible as accidental strips. I’ll convert the plant into an organic cutout and isolate the Flatiron as a deliberate architectural counterweight, preserving the cosmic ground around the assembled self.

The inspected canvas now has a convincing central body and orbiting selves, but the city identity is visually lost behind the botanical spine. I’ll bring the Flatiron forward as a lower-left urban anchor and add a small, tilted Moulin Rouge fragment as the social/performed voice of “I.”

The latest canvas has a compelling lunar stage and a clear central “I,” but the flamingo still carries a rectangular paper field and the blue self-portrait carries a gray surround. I’ll cut both into cleaner silhouettes so the orbiting identities feel assembled in the same visual language.

The inspected canvas now clearly stages “I” as a historical body surrounded by botanical, civic, performative, animal, and planetary selves. The remaining distraction is the botanical cutout’s broad white perimeter, so I’ll tighten that silhouette once more without disturbing the central figure.
notes.error: This trim creates 9 pieces and would exceed the 24-piece limit.

notes.note: The visual inspection shows the composition is readable and balanced, but the botanical cutout’s white edge dominates the central field. Since further trimming would exceed the piece limit, I’ll remove that distracting layer and let the central witness sit directly against the cosmic ground; the surrounding selves will carry the collage’s plurality.

The latest canvas is legible and strong, but the central Frederick Douglass image still reads as a large beige paper shape rather than a body emerging from the lunar ground. I’ll make one final silhouette trim around the portrait and then use the remaining turn to inspect the finished result.

The final canvas is finished: a central historical witness stands on the lunar threshold, while the surrounding portrait, flamingo, city, performance poster, and planetary Earth form a dispersed community of selves. The title and statement are present and the composition is visually coherent.
